ENT Clinical Note
Valerie Cole  |  DOB 19 Sep 1993  |  Video consult with Dr Smith

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure  
  – Main concern: gradually worsening anxiety over the last ≈2 months, temporally related to starting a new, highly stressful job.  
  – No food, medication, or environmental trigger reported.

• Symptom timeline and progression  
  – Daily anticipatory dread each morning before work; difficulty leaving the house.  
  – Marked insomnia (bed 22-23 h, sleep ≈3-4 h; shallow); wakes early with racing heart.  
  – Morning palpitations described as “irregular” lasting a few-10 min.  
  – Progressive functional impact: low energy, diminished enjoyment of exercise/social activities, strained concentration at work.

• ENT-relevant symptoms  
  – Throat tightness/closure sensation: not reported.  
  – Voice change/hoarseness: not reported.  
  – Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: not reported.  
  – Nasal/ocular symptoms: not reported.  
  – Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: not reported.  
  – Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: not reported.  
  – Ear pain/hearing changes, neck pain/swelling: not reported.

• Relevant past episodes / treatments  
  – No prior similar episodes; no ED visits; no medication or injection therapy taken to date.  

• Allergies and current medications  
  – Drug/food/environmental allergies: not documented.  
  – Current regular medicines: none documented.  
  – OTC / PRN: none documented.

• Social context  
  – Lives with parents; good family support.  
  – Alcohol: binge drinking most Fri/Sat; occasional weekday wine.  
  – Tobacco: occasional smoker; no recreational drugs.

Objective:
• Observable swelling: none reported.  
• Airway/breathing: no stridor, dyspnea, or voice change reported.  
• Mental status: anxious, distressed but coherent; no suicidal ideation.  
• Vitals and physical examination: Not recorded (video consultation).  
• Presence of another person: patient alone during consult.

Assessment:
Working clinical impression  
– Suspected adjustment disorder with anxiety (early generalized anxiety picture) precipitated by workplace stress; possible emerging mixed anxiety-depressive features.

Evidence summary  
• Clear temporal link to new stressful job; pervasive worry and somatic tension (palpitations, insomnia).  
• Functional impairment (social withdrawal, anhedonia) but still attends work; no suicidal ideation.

DDx (aligned with transcript)  
1. Adjustment disorder / early Generalized Anxiety Disorder – high likelihood; onset within 2 months of identifiable stressor, daily excessive worry, insomnia.  
2. Major depressive episode with anxious distress – moderate likelihood; reports persistent low mood, loss of enjoyment, fatigue; no suicidality.  
3. Hyperthyroidism – low-medium likelihood; palpitations and insomnia overlap; will screen via blood tests.  
   Opposing evidence: no weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor.

Plan:
• Provided NHS self-referral link for talking therapy (CBT-based).  
• Advised evidence-based online anxiety resources; sleep-hygiene guidance to be sent via patient information sheet.  
• Ordered basic blood work (FBC, TSH, U&E, glucose, ferritin) to exclude metabolic/thyroid or anaemic contributors to palpitations and fatigue.  
• Follow-up: phone/GP appointment 1 week after labs to review results and symptom progression.  
• Safety-netting: call GP sooner or attend ED if  
  – palpitations are prolonged, associated with chest pain, syncope, or breathlessness;  
  – escalation of anxiety to inability to work or perform daily activities;  
  – emergence of suicidal thoughts.  
• Medication: none started now; discussed that pharmacotherapy (e.g., SSRI) can be considered if therapy alone insufficient.  
• Lifestyle advice: limit binge alcohol; gradual return to exercise; smoking cessation support if desired.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: full allergy list; current medication list with dose/route/frequency; detailed ENT/airway examination; vital signs.  
● Conflicts transcript vs DDx: none identified.  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; no major inaudible segments.
